mission.title: kyverno: [Bug] [CLI] CRDs not loaded when specified in tests with ClusterResource
mission.description: [Bug] [CLI] CRDs not loaded when specified in tests with ClusterResource. This issue affects 20+ users.

steps.title: Identify kyverno troubleshoot symptoms
steps.description:
Check for the issue in your kyverno deployment:
```bash
kubectl get pods -n kyverno -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno -n kyverno --tail=100 | grep -i error
```
Look for errors or warnings in the logs that may indicate the issue.

steps.title: Review kyverno configuration
steps.description:
Inspect the relevant kyverno configuration:
```bash
kubectl get all -n kyverno -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno
kubectl get configmap -n kyverno -l app.kubernetes.io/part-of=kyverno
```
When writing tests for a CEL-based policy that acts on CRs and providing the CRD through a ClusterResource, the CRD is not correctly mapped, which causes the test to fail with the following error:

```
Error: failed to run test (failed to apply

steps.title: Apply the fix for [Bug] [CLI] CRDs not loaded when specified in tests with…
steps.description:
**Chainsaw** is currently the main alternative for end-to-end testing of the newer policy types, while kyverno test is intended for fast, offline unit/regression testing. So Chainsaw can work as a workaround for CRD-dependent tests, but it doesn't really replace kyverno test.

It may also be worth
```yaml
Error: failed to run test (failed to apply policies on resource <resource> (failed to map gvk to gvr <group>/<version>, Kind=<Kind> (no matches for kind "<Kind>" in version "<group>/<version>")
```

steps.title: Confirm [Bug] [CLI] CRDs not loaded when specified in… is resolved
steps.description:
Verify the fix by checking that the original error no longer occurs:
```bash
kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=kyverno -n kyverno --tail=50 --since=5m
kubectl get events -n kyverno --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -10
```
Confirm that the issue symptoms are gone.

resolution.summary: **Chainsaw** is currently the main alternative for end-to-end testing of the newer policy types, while kyverno test is intended for fast, offline unit/regression testing. So Chainsaw can work as a workaround for CRD-dependent tests, but it doesn't really replace kyverno test.
